title: Body parts split: bro split vs Gentleman Split
summary: NH defends body part splits as the most flexible template, distinguishing the bad 'bro split' (one muscle per day, once a week) from his 'gentleman split' (synergistic muscle groups, several hits per week). He contrasts them on synergy, frequency and injury prevention, arguing many PPL and upper/lower users are already running body part splits.
claims: A body part split is the most flexible and optimal template for bodybuilding; listing pros and cons it always comes out on top
YouTube fitness hates body part splits because it confuses them with the bro split, which is the worst template; anything beats a bro split but nothing beats a gentleman split
The same principle can be immensely good or bad depending only on how you apply it
Dedicating a whole day to a small muscle like triceps is abysmal: you either finish too fast or pile up junk volume it cannot recover from
Bro splits were popularized by enhanced athletes, for whom lazy programming still works; it will not work for naturals
Resting three minutes between triceps sets instead of training something else is wasted time
Gentleman split: pair synergistic muscles, e.g. triceps with chest and shoulders, which also dictates exercise selection: horizontal and vertical presses as pillars

Build the day on compound movements because they move a lot of weight, involve many muscles, accumulate tonnage quickly and drive progression, then add isolation like flyes, triceps extensions and rear delt work
Many people doing push/pull/legs or upper/lower are actually doing body part splits without realizing it
Bro splits train each muscle once a week, which is not enough for a natural who can handle more
PEDs extend the window of elevated protein synthesis, so naturals may need more frequency than enhanced lifters
Enhanced and natural lifters' volumes are not very different; the enhanced get their extra tonnage from drugs and are much stronger
Frequency must differ by body part; training triceps with the same frequency as legs ignores differences in size and durability
Training abs once a week will never give a thick six-pack
Compounds must be practiced 2-3 times a week to avoid neurological regression and to drive growth; once a week risks stagnation
When bro-splitters stall they just add sets instead of weight, which is not proper natural progression
The 'skip leg day' meme comes from bro splits; cramming all lower body volume into one weekly day makes it unrecoverable and hated
Leg days made of leg extensions without squats and deadlifts will not build big natural legs
A gentleman split hits muscles several times per week at upper/lower-like frequency with varying intensity: heavy, moderate, pump days
Pros on bro splits use machines and low intensity to avoid injury, because cramming all volume into one day at high intensity would snap them up
Many get shoulder pain benching 3x/week even with recovery; putting all that volume and intensity in one day risks permanent injury
Rear delts are small muscles whose number one pillar is frequency, not volume or intensity; once a week will not grow them
Ab days and lower back days are idiotic: train abs every day and lower back at least twice a week for structural integrity
A gentleman split leaves room for daily leg raises, lower back work on every lower day and prehab such as a hamstring/glute day with hyperextensions
exercises: small muscle needs frequency; injury prevention
